authoredSolutions.41: For ionic solids the melting point follows the lattice enthalpy, which rises with the charges on the ions and falls as the ions get larger. LiF against LiCl: the cation is the same and \(F^{-}\) is much smaller than \(Cl^{-}\), so LiF has the larger lattice enthalpy and the higher melting point (about \(848^{\circ}C\) against \(610^{\circ}C\)). MgO against NaCl: \(Mg^{2+}\) and \(O^{2-}\) each carry a double charge, so the lattice enthalpy of MgO is about four times that of NaCl and it melts far higher (about \(2850^{\circ}C\) against \(801^{\circ}C\)). So LiF > LiCl and MgO > NaCl, option (B).

Split on the modulus.
\[\textbf{Case } x<5:\ (x+1)^2-(x-5)=\frac{27}{4}\Rightarrow x^2+x+6=\frac{27}{4}\Rightarrow x^2+x-\frac34=0.\]
This gives \(x=\dfrac{-1\pm 2}{2}=\dfrac12,\,-\dfrac32\); both satisfy \(x<5\), so \(2\) roots.
\[\textbf{Case } x\ge 5:\ (x+1)^2+(x-5)=\frac{27}{4}\Rightarrow x^2+3x-\frac{43}{4}=0.\]
Here \(x=\dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt{52}}{2}\approx 2.1,\,-5.1\), neither is \(\ge 5\), so no roots.
Hence the total number of real roots is \(\boxed{2}\).

Groups \(A,B,C\) are distinct, each non-empty, with \(|C|\le 3\). Fix \(|C|=c\): choose \(C\) in \(\binom{10}{c}\) ways and distribute the remaining \(10-c\) students onto \(A,B\) with both non-empty in \(2^{10-c}-2\) ways.
\[c=1:\ \binom{10}{1}(2^{9}-2)=10\cdot 510=5100,\]
\[c=2:\ \binom{10}{2}(2^{8}-2)=45\cdot 254=11430,\]

Given \(a f(x)+\alpha f\!\left(\tfrac1x\right)=bx+\dfrac{\beta}{x}\). Replace \(x\) by \(\tfrac1x\):
\[\alpha f(x)+a f\!\left(\tfrac1x\right)=\frac{b}{x}+\beta x.\]
Add the two equations:
\[(a+\alpha)\left(f(x)+f\!\left(\tfrac1x\right)\right)=(b+\beta)\left(x+\tfrac1x\right).\]
With \(a+\alpha=1\) and \(b+\beta=2\),
\[\frac{f(x)+f\!\left(\tfrac1x\right)}{x+\tfrac1x}=\frac{b+\beta}{a+\alpha}=\frac{2}{1}=\boxed{2}.\]

The data are nine \(1\)'s and one \(k\). Mean \(=\dfrac{9+k}{10}\), and
\[\sigma^2=\frac{9\cdot 1^2+k^2}{10}-\left(\frac{9+k}{10}\right)^2=\frac{10(9+k^2)-(9+k)^2}{100}=\frac{9(k-1)^2}{100}.\]
Require \(\sigma^2<10\):
\[\frac{9(k-1)^2}{100}<10\Rightarrow (k-1)^2<\frac{1000}{9}=111.1\Rightarrow |k-1|<10.54.\]
So \(k<11.54\); the largest natural number is \(k=\boxed{11}\).

Write the lines in symmetric form. Line 1: \(x-\lambda=2y-1=-2z\) has point \(P_1=(\lambda,\tfrac12,0)\) and direction \(\vec d_1=(2,1,-1)\). Line 2: \(x=y+2\lambda=z-\lambda\) has point \(P_2=(0,-2\lambda,\lambda)\) and direction \(\vec d_2=(1,1,1)\).
\[\vec d_1\times\vec d_2=(2,-3,1),\qquad |\vec d_1\times\vec d_2|=\sqrt{14}.\]
With \(P_2-P_1=(-\lambda,\,-2\lambda-\tfrac12,\,\lambda)\), the projection is \((P_2-P_1)\cdot(2,-3,1)=5\lambda+\tfrac32\).
\[\text{d}=\frac{|5\lambda+\tfrac32|}{\sqrt{14}}=\frac{\sqrt7}{2\sqrt2}=\frac{\sqrt{14}}{4}\Rightarrow\Big|5\lambda+\tfrac32\Big|=\frac{7}{2}.\]
Thus \(5\lambda=2\) or \(5\lambda=-5\); the integer solution is \(\lambda=-1\), so \(|\lambda|=\boxed{1}\).

By the Vandermonde identity,
\[\sum_{i=0}^{k}\binom{10}{i}\binom{15}{k-i}=\binom{25}{k},\qquad \sum_{i=0}^{k+1}\binom{12}{i}\binom{13}{k+1-i}=\binom{25}{k+1}.\]
Hence the total is
\[\binom{25}{k}+\binom{25}{k+1}=\binom{26}{k+1}.\]
This binomial coefficient is largest when \(k+1=13\), i.e. \(k=\boxed{12}\).

Let the G.P. be \(a,ar,ar^2,ar^3\). The product of the first three terms is \((ar)^3=1\Rightarrow ar=1\).
With \(S=a+ar+ar^2+ar^3\) and \(S'=\dfrac1a+\dfrac1{ar}+\dfrac1{ar^2}+\dfrac1{ar^3}\), one gets \(\dfrac{S}{S'}=a^2r^3=(ar)^2 r=r\).
\[r=\frac{S}{S'}=\frac{65/12}{65/18}=\frac{18}{12}=\frac32.\]
Then \(a=\dfrac1r=\dfrac23\), and the third term \(\alpha=ar^2=\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac94=\dfrac32\).
Therefore \(2\alpha=\boxed{3}\).

Circle \((x-2)^2+(y-3)^2=25\) has centre \(C=(2,3)\); at \(P=(5,7)\) the radius \(CP\) has slope \(\dfrac{7-3}{5-2}=\dfrac43\).
Normal (through \(P\), slope \(\tfrac43\)) meets the \(x\)-axis: \(0-7=\tfrac43(x-5)\Rightarrow x=-\tfrac14\).
Tangent (through \(P\), slope \(-\tfrac34\)) meets the \(x\)-axis: \(0-7=-\tfrac34(x-5)\Rightarrow x=\tfrac{43}{3}\).
The triangle has its base on the \(x\)-axis from \(-\tfrac14\) to \(\tfrac{43}{3}\) and apex \(P\) at height \(7\):
\[A=\frac12\left(\frac{43}{3}+\frac14\right)\cdot 7=\frac12\cdot\frac{175}{12}\cdot 7=\frac{1225}{24}.\]
Thus \(24A=\boxed{1225}\).
